text:
infra-bot: Incident created for tenant `Voltly` — spike of 5xx/timeouts on hosted inference (autocreated from support ticket #98721).

priya: Customer reports repeated 504s and slow responses since ~22:10 UTC. Support ticket: https://support.redwood/98721. They say it affects their checkout flow, lots of small requests but some long sequences.

zheng: Oncall here, looking at metrics now. Request queue depth spiked to ~11k for the Voltly route at 22:12 UTC, continuous-batcher backlog grew from 200 -> 6.5k. p95 token latency jumped to 8s, p99 to 23s. Seeing a big drop in dequeue throughput.

marco: Can you paste the tail logs for batcher? suspect batching window + KV cache churn.

zheng: Pasting relevant logs snippet:```
22:11:58 batcher-voltly[i-7f9] INFO enqueue req_id=abc123 len=450
22:12:02 batcher-voltly[i-7f9] WARN kvcache-miss tenant=voltly key=chat:kv:xyz
22:12:09 batcher-voltly[i-7f9] ERROR dequeue_timeout waited=300ms queue_len=10240
22:12:10 router[i-2a1] ERROR upstream 504 tenant=voltly route=/api/v1/generate
```

priya: Customer says failures are intermittent but high frequency, started after a deploy? they noted increased traffic from an internal monitoring job.

jamie: I see a canary deploy completed at 22:05 that changed default batch_wait_ms from 50 -> 80ms for all batchers. That increases batching window and can amplify queueing when requests are bursty.

marco: Immediate mitigations: 1) reduce batch_wait_ms for Voltly batcher to 5ms, 2) temporarily scale batcher replicas for that tenant, 3) enable per-tenant queue limit to reject excess traffic before it piles up. I'll handle 1&2.

zheng: Executing now:```
# reduce batching window for Voltly
curl -X PATCH "https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/batchers/voltly" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"batch_wait_ms":5}'

# scale batcher deployment
kubectl scale deploy/batcher-voltly -n inference --replicas=6
```

marco: Also flipping route to fallback model variant (smaller seq length) for Voltly to reduce per-request token work:```
POST /api/v1/routes/voltly/fallback
{ "fallback_model": "redwood-small-v1" }
```

priya: Support will message the customer with a temporary mitigation note: reduced batching + scale. Asking SRE to confirm expected recovery window.

zheng: After change: queue depth dropped from 11k -> 900 within 45s, dequeue throughput normalized. 5xx rate reduced to baseline within 3 minutes. Marking incident as mitigated for customer.

jamie: Root cause hypothesis: the larger global batch_wait_ms from the canary made the system more susceptible to sudden low-qps long-sequence bursts (monitoring job) which caused continuous-batcher backlog and KV cache churn. Need postmortem.

marco: Proposed long-term fixes: - per-tenant adaptive batch windows - per-tenant queue depth caps + graceful reject (429) - smarter admission control to prioritize short seq requests - deploy circuit-breaker for KV spin-up storms

priya: Logged follow-up steps in ticket #98721 and support will coordinate a scheduled postmortem with Voltly. Notifying account manager.

zheng: I'll open an incident PR with timings and add traces. tagging for postmortem: @marco @jamie @priya. :white_check_mark: 

infra-bot: Incident updated — mitigations applied, status: mitigated, follow-up required.
